rules.title: Intel XPU unavailable in PyTorch
rules.tip: PyTorch XPU is not available (torch={torch_version}). Install a PyTorch XPU build (e.g., torch==2.13.0+xpu on Python 3.13) and check your Intel Arc GPU driver/runtime.

rules.title: PyTorch version differs from 2.13.0+xpu
rules.tip: Detected torch=={torch_version} (Python {python_version}). Prebuilt Windows binaries for ComfyUI-Intel-Arc-XPU require Python 3.13 + torch==2.13.0+xpu.

rules.title: Conflicting extension detected (comfyui-xpu-backend)
rules.tip: custom_nodes/comfyui-xpu-backend can conflict with OmniXPU / ComfyUI-Intel-Arc-XPU. Remove or disable the legacy extension and restart ComfyUI.

rules.title: Running ComfyUI without native XPU acceleration
rules.tip: Install OmniXPU (https://github.com/intel/llm-scaler/tree/main/omni on Linux or https://github.com/wildersa/ComfyUI-Intel-Arc-XPU on Windows) to enable native SYCL/oneDNN kernels, comfy-kitchen XPU backend (INT8/FP8/ConvRot), and DynamicVRAM.

rules.title: Native XPU binaries (omni_xpu_kernel) are not installed yet
rules.tip: The OmniXPU Python extension is present, but omni_xpu_kernel is missing from this Python environment. Complete binary setup for your platform (install.ps1 / install.py on Windows, or intel/llm-scaler omni stack on Linux).

rules.title: comfy_kitchen XPU backend is inactive
rules.tip: omni_xpu_kernel is present, but comfy_kitchen's 'xpu' backend is unavailable or disabled. Native INT8/W4A8/ConvRot kernels will fall back to slower PyTorch execution; check comfy-kitchen-xpu-runtime and startup logs.

rules.title: DynamicVRAM is disabled
rules.tip: For heavy/video workflows that exceed free VRAM, add --enable-dynamic-vram to ComfyUI launch arguments.

rules.title: Free XPU VRAM below 8% ({free_vram_mb} MB / {total_vram_mb} MB)
rules.tip: XPU memory headroom is tight with DynamicVRAM disabled. Enable --enable-dynamic-vram (or add --reserve-vram 2 if you hit OOM during VAE/sampling).

rules.title: Windows Shared GPU Memory spike ({shared_vram_mb} MB)
rules.tip: ComfyUI overflowed dedicated XPU VRAM into system RAM over PCIe (WDDM shared memory), which can severely slow down sampling. Enable --enable-dynamic-vram in ComfyUI launch arguments.

rules.title: Windows Shared GPU Memory spike ({shared_vram_mb} MB)
rules.tip: Dedicated XPU VRAM spilled into WDDM Shared GPU Memory even with DynamicVRAM active. Try adding --reserve-vram 2 (or 4 for heavy video) or using smaller int8_convrot weights.

rules.title: Host RAM weight staging blocked (--disable-pinned-memory)
rules.tip: Running DynamicVRAM with --disable-pinned-memory disables host RAM staging, forcing large models to re-read weights from disk during swaps.

rules.title: Using PyTorch SDPA on Intel Arc Battlemage
rules.tip: OMNI_ATTN_BACKEND is set to 'torch' (PyTorch SDPA). Setting OMNI_ATTN_BACKEND=cute on Battlemage (bmg) typically improves speed ~10% (switch back to 'torch' if visual artifacts appear).

rules.title: FP8 diffusion weights active ({loaded_fp8_model_names})
rules.tip: Intel Arc Battlemage (Xe2) executes FP8 via dequantization/emulation rather than native XMX INT8. If an int8_convrot variant exists for this model, switching to it usually delivers higher it/s and lower VRAM.

rules.pattern: XPU out of memory|Allocation on device \d+ would exceed allowed memory|OutOfMemoryError.*xpu
rules.title: XPU Out of Memory (DynamicVRAM disabled)
rules.tip: Add --enable-dynamic-vram to your ComfyUI launch arguments to enable XPU weight offloading.

rules.pattern: XPU out of memory|Allocation on device \d+ would exceed allowed memory|OutOfMemoryError.*xpu
rules.title: Memory spike caused OOM under DynamicVRAM
rules.tip: DynamicVRAM is enabled without extra headroom (--reserve-vram). Add --reserve-vram 2 (or 4 for heavy video) to leave room for KSampler/VAE activations.

rules.pattern: XPU out of memory|Allocation on device \d+ would exceed allowed memory|OutOfMemoryError.*xpu
rules.title: XPU Out of Memory during execution
rules.tip: Even with DynamicVRAM + --reserve-vram {reserve_vram_gb}, allocation spiked past free VRAM. Try lowering resolution/frames, using INT8/FP8 weights, or increasing --reserve-vram.

rules.pattern: Attention backend 'comfy kitchen attention' is unavailable
rules.title: Workflow configured for CUDA-only attention
rules.tip: This workflow originated on NVIDIA ('comfy kitchen attention'). Switch ModelAttentionBackend to 'pytorch attention' in the workflow.

rules.pattern: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled|No CUDA GPUs are available|Found no NVIDIA driver|not on CUDA
rules.title: Node or library attempted to use CUDA on Intel XPU
rules.tip: A workflow node/extension called CUDA directly (for example SageAttention, FlashAttention, or CUDA sparse attention). Replace or bypass it with standard PyTorch attention.

rules.title: OmniXPU patch conflict detected (using stock fallback)
rules.tip: A ComfyUI update changed an internal hook, so OmniXPU safely fell back to stock ComfyUI behavior. Check your OmniXPU / ComfyUI-Intel-Arc-XPU extension for updates.

rules.pattern: experimental capability-driven BMG D128 CUTE route enabled
rules.title: Experimental CUTE BMG route enabled
rules.tip: OMNI_ATTN_BACKEND=cute took the experimental BMG D128 route. If you observe visual artifacts, set OMNI_ATTN_BACKEND=torch and restart ComfyUI.

rules.title: FP8 quantization detected in logs
rules.tip: FP8 weights run via dequantization/emulation on Intel Arc (no dedicated FP8 XMX hardware). Prefer an int8_convrot variant when available for faster steps and lower VRAM.

rules.pattern: Model WAN21 prepared for dynamic VRAM loading\. .*\b0 patches attached\.
rules.title: Wan 2.2 running without 4-step LightX2V LoRA (0 patches attached)
rules.tip: WAN21 loaded with 0 LoRA patches attached. In the built-in Wan 2.2 template, the 4-step LightX2V LoRA group is bypassed by default, running 20 steps at cfg=3.5 (~11.5 min on Arc B70). For ~80–95s generation, un-bypass the 4-step LoRA group and set steps=4 (2+2) with cfg=1.0.

rules.title: ONNX node configured for CUDA ({class_type})
rules.tip: This node uses '{matched_value}', which is unavailable on Intel Arc XPU. Switch the provider widget to 'CPUExecutionProvider' (or 'DmlExecutionProvider' on Windows).

rules.title: Preprocess/Vision node hardcoded to 'cuda' ({class_type})
rules.tip: This node has its device widget set to 'cuda', which raises 'Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled' on Intel Arc XPU. Change the device widget to 'cpu' (and precision to 'fp32' when running on CPU).

rules.title: GGUF model loader active ({class_type})
rules.tip: GGUF weights dequantize block-by-block in generic PyTorch and bypass native Intel Arc XPU kernels (comfy-kitchen-xpu-runtime XMX INT8/ConvRot) and DynamicVRAM staged pinning. Prefer native UNETLoader / CLIPLoader with .safetensors (int8_convrot or fp8_scaled).

rules.title: CUDA/Triton-specific node or backend in workflow ({class_type})
rules.tip: This node is configured for '{matched_value}'. On Intel Arc XPU, select 'pytorch attention' (accelerated automatically by OmniXPU) and bypass CUDA-only TorchCompile/SageAttention nodes.

rules.title: Full-batch ImageUpscaleWithModel active in workflow
rules.tip: In multi-frame video workflows, ImageUpscaleWithModel upscales all frames at once in VRAM and can cause OOM or heavy Shared GPU Memory spills. Consider bypassing it or using a tiled upscaler for video.

rules.title: WanAnimate2Cache device set to 'gpu'
rules.tip: WanAnimate2Cache is storing pose K/V tensors on 'gpu'. For longer driving videos or tighter VRAM headroom, switch WanAnimate2Cache device to 'cpu'.

rules.title: FP8 diffusion checkpoint selected in loader ({class_type})
rules.tip: Intel Arc Battlemage (Xe2) emulates FP8 via dequantization rather than native XMX INT8. If an int8_convrot version of '{target_object}' is available, switching to it uses native XMX INT8 via comfy-kitchen-xpu-runtime.
